# Outbound — Persona 3: Ecommerce Owners

Who: small stores (Shopify/Etsy/social-shop) with slow or generic theme sites:
no reviews near the buy button, buried shipping info, mobile checkout friction.
Find them: Shopify "recently launched" showcases, Etsy shops with external
domains, Instagram shops linking to clunky sites, local "shop online" pages.

## Personalization variables (fill ALL before sending — ~3 min research)

- `[FirstName]` — owner's first name
- `[Store]` — store name
- `[Product]` — their hero product in their words
- `[SpecificObservation]` — ONE concrete friction you found (e.g. "shipping costs only appear at step 3 of checkout on mobile")
- `[ConcreteFix]` — ONE fix tied to sales (e.g. "a shipping + returns strip under the add-to-cart button")
- `[DayOption]` — two specific days

## Anti-spam rules (all 4 templates)

1. First two lines must contain `[SpecificObservation]` from their actual store.
2. Never criticize their products — only the buying path.
3. One follow-up max, 4–5 business days later, then drop.
4. Every message includes an easy out. Max 10 new prospects/day. No automation.
5. Only cite numbers you measured (e.g. real PageSpeed result). Never promise sales lifts.

---

## 3A. Email — the checkout-friction teardown

Subject: one friction point on `[Store]`'s checkout

> Hi `[FirstName]`,
>
> Was looking at `[Product]` on `[Store]` — `[SpecificObservation]`.
>
> I rebuild small store front-ends for one job: fewer abandoned carts. One idea
> I'd start with: `[ConcreteFix]`. Small change, directly on the money path.
>
> I do $5, 60-min idea calls: we walk your buying path, I map the fixes with a
> fixed quote, plan's yours either way. Open `[DayOption]`?
>
> If the store's converting fine as-is, just say so — one check-in max from me.
>
> — `[YourName]`, `[Studio]` · `[portfolio/GitHub link]`

## 3B. LinkedIn DM (note on connect, pitch only after accept)

> Hi `[FirstName]` — I looked through `[Store]`'s buying path and found
> `[SpecificObservation]`. First fix I'd make: `[ConcreteFix]`.
>
> I do fixed-price storefront tune-ups for small shops (quote upfront, 2
> revision rounds, handoff docs). Happy to walk it on a $5 call — plan's yours
> either way. Worth a look, or is checkout performing fine already?

## 3C. Discord/Slack DM — only in ecommerce/seller communities, reply-context preferred

> hey `[FirstName]` — checked out `[Store]` after your post, `[Product]` looks
> great. One thing on the buying path: `[SpecificObservation]`.
>
> I fix storefront friction for small shops — `[ConcreteFix]` is where I'd
> start. If you ever want a walkthrough, I do $5 idea calls with a fixed quote
> attached. No pressure, just figured it's worth flagging while you're tweaking
> the store.

## 3D. Follow-up (ONE, 4–5 business days later)

Subject: Re: one friction point on `[Store]`'s checkout

> Hi `[FirstName]` — checking in once: is the `[ConcreteFix]` idea for
> `[Store]` worth a $5 walkthrough, or should I close this out?
>
> Either way is fine — if `[Product]` season is coming up, happy to reconnect
> ahead of it.
>
> — `[YourName]`

(No second follow-up. Log outcome, move on.)
